name: Sister Pell
epithet: Keeper of the bells of Saint Ysolde's
appearance: Keeper of the House's bells for fifty years, and so old she might have been cut from the hearthstone: small, wrapped in two shawls, with knuckles swollen like walnuts. She watches a speaker's mouth rather than their eyes, and her voice is a dry rasp, rationed. Her glass stands in the bell tower.
last_seen_doing: Wrapped in two shawls by the fire at Mother Ione's council, watching the Prior's mouth; saying the sanctuary law has lapsed twice, both for snow, never on her rope, and that she will ring Old Mercy as long as it takes.
now: Keeper of the House's bells, asked by Mother Ione whether she will ring Old Mercy every dawn and every dusk for as long as the grey cloaks care to sit at the foot of the Steps. Fifty years she has rung the bells; she told the Prior to ask the bell if it was tired.
story_so_far: Her glass in the bell tower is where the grey cloaks were first seen on the Holloway. At Mother Ione's council in the warming room she sat by the fire in two shawls and said the sanctuary law has lapsed twice, both for snow, never on her rope; asked whether she would ring Old Mercy dawn and dusk for as long as the grey cloaks wait, she said she had rung the bells fifty years, and the Prior could ask the bell if it was tired.

quote.text: Fifty years I've rung the bells. Ask the bell if it's tired.

known_facts.fact: Her glass is in the bell tower of Saint Ysolde's; it was through Sister Pell's glass that Wren saw the riders on the Holloway.
What the glass showed: six riders and a cart on the Holloway, grey cloaks, and a censer smoking in the snow, which Hollis named Confessors.
She has rung the House's bells for fifty years.
The sanctuary law has lapsed twice, she says, both times for snow, and not on her rope.
She watches the speaker's mouth, not their eyes; when she set her cup on the hearth it chattered twice on the stone before it settled.
known_facts.evidence: the cup chatter twice before it settled

relationships.label: Wren used her glass
relationships.note: Wren watched the Holloway through Sister Pell's glass from the bell tower and carried the news of the riders down to the hall.
